cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him. God calls him 'Son of man' and tells him to pose a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel. A riddle from the LORD Himself, friend, so pull up a stool and lean in.
Here's the riddle: a great eagle with great wings, long pinions and feathers of many colors comes to Lebanon. That eagle didn't fly in, friend, he made an ENTRANCE.

cards.question: What does this great eagle take in Lebanon?
The eagle plucks off the cedar's topmost shoot. Where does he carry it?

cards.text: He plants that shoot in a city of traders. Then he takes some of the seed of the land and plants that too, like a gardener who actually read the back of the packet.

cards.question: The eagle plants the seed of the land in fertile soil, by abundant ___.
The eagle's seed grows into a tall tree that towers over everything around it.

cards.text: It sprouts into a spreading vine, low in height, with its roots staying right where it stood. Low but spreading, friend, which is also how I'd describe my mustache.

cards.question: Which way do this low vine's branches turn?

answers.text: Toward the eagle who planted it

cards.text: But hold on, there's ANOTHER great eagle with great wings and many feathers. Two big birds and one little vine? I'm nervous already.

cards.question: When the second great eagle shows up, the vine bends its roots toward him.
Why does the vine stretch its branches out to the second eagle?

answers.text: So he might plant it higher
So he might carry it off

cards.text: And here's the wild part: that vine was ALREADY planted in good soil by abundant waters, set up to bear fruit and become a splendid vine. That's sitting at your desk, on the company laptop, emailing your resume to the competition.
Then God asks it straight out: 'Will it flourish?' And friend, I don't love this vine's chances.

cards.question: What does God say will happen to this vine that reached for the second eagle?

answers.text: It will be uprooted and wither
It will grow into a cedar
It will be moved to Lebanon

cards.question: God says it will take a strong arm and many people to pull this vine up by its roots.

cards.text: Then God asks again: even if it's transplanted, will it flourish? New address, same vine, friend.

cards.question: Even if the vine is transplanted, it will completely wither when the ___ wind strikes.

cards.text: It withers right on the bed where it sprouted. Two eagles, one vine, a WHOLE lot of feathers, and next God tells Ezekiel what it all means.

The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, and God tells him to ask this rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Then God hands over the answer key, and friend, I am SO relieved.

cards.question: In God's explanation, who comes to Jerusalem and carries off its king and officials?

cards.text: So that flashy first eagle is the king of Babylon, and the topmost shoot is Jerusalem's king and officials, carried off to Babylon. I KNEW those feathers were royalty.

cards.question: Then the king of Babylon takes a member of Jerusalem's royal family. What does he do with him?

answers.text: Makes a covenant with him under oath
Makes him a servant in his palace
Puts him in chains in the city

cards.text: That's the seed the eagle planted. Then the king of Babylon carries away the leading men of the land, so the kingdom is brought low and can't lift itself up.

cards.question: The kingdom that was brought low would survive only by keeping the king of Babylon's ___.

cards.text: But this king rebels against Babylon. And friend, remember that vine stretching its branches toward the second eagle?

cards.question: Where does this king send his envoys when he rebels against Babylon?
This king sends his envoys to Egypt to ask for ___ and a large ___.

cards.text: Then God asks, 'Can he break a covenant and yet escape?' And God answers it Himself: as surely as He lives, this king isn't getting away with it.

cards.question: Where does God say this king who broke the covenant will die?
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, has a mighty army and a vast horde, and God says Pharaoh will help this king in battle.

cards.text: God says this king gave his hand in pledge, then did all these things, and he will not escape. That's shaking on the deal, then texting the other guy before you even make it back to your car.
Then God says He'll bring down on this king's head 'My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.' God calls that oath and that covenant His OWN, friend.

cards.question: God says, 'I will spread My ___ over him and catch him in My snare.'

cards.text: God says He'll bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the treason he committed against God Himself.

cards.question: This king's choice troops fall by the sword. What happens to the ones who survive?

answers.text: They are scattered to every wind
They are taken as slaves to Egypt
They are sent home to Jerusalem

cards.text: Then God says, 'Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.' But don't close the cookie box yet, friend, because the cedar from the riddle is coming back.

cards.question: Back in the riddle, an eagle took the top of the cedar. This time, who takes a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar?

cards.text: The LORD plucks a tender sprig from its topmost shoots and sets it out. The cedar's back, and this time the gardener is the LORD.

cards.question: Where does the LORD plant this tender sprig?

answers.text: On the mountain heights of Israel

cards.question: God says the tender sprig will bear branches, yield fruit and become a majestic ___.
The branches of this majestic cedar give shade, but only eagles get to nest under it.

cards.text: Then God says all the trees of the field will know that He is the LORD, and He says, 'I bring the tall tree down.'

cards.question: Right after bringing the tall tree down, what does God say He does with the low tree?
God says He keeps the green tree green.

cards.text: Then God says, 'I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.' Friend, take it from a worn-out stamper pulled out of the back of a junk drawer: He really does make the withered tree flourish.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess which wind is named (east, north or south). Nothing on the earlier cards helps the baker reason it out, so this tests wording they haven't seen and comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card cites only Ezekiel 17:10, but it also says 'next God tells Ezekiel what it all means.' That tells the content of 17:11-12, which this card doesn't cite. Stop 2 card 1 then tells the same moment again.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card cites only Ezekiel 17:21, but it also says 'the cedar from the riddle is coming back.' That tells the content of 17:22, which this card doesn't cite.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Saying 'the cedar from the riddle is coming back' signals that the sprig will become a cedar. That gives away the answer to stop 3 card 9 ('become a majestic ___', answer cedar) and rules out the wrong answers vine and willow.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'The cedar's back' comes right before card 9, which asks what the sprig becomes (cedar). This setup line gives away the answer and rules out vine and willow.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The LORD plucks a tender sprig from its topmost shoots and sets it out' tells the moment as something happening now. In Ezekiel 17:22 it is God's promise in the future tense: 'I will take… I will set it out. I will pluck…'. The retelling should keep it as what God says He will do.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
